prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first: do you want a specific name(s) of local lawyers, or do you want guidance so you can pick the right lawyer yourself? If you want names, I can pull together a short list of experienced Pleasanton/Tri‑Valley personal injury attorneys with contact details and ratings.

Meanwhile, here’s concise, practical guidance so you hire the right lawyer for your car‑accident injury case.

What matters most when choosing a personal injury lawyer
- Relevant experience: pick an attorney who handles car‑accident cases (not a generalist) and has won settlements/trials like yours (rear‑end, T‑bone, catastrophic injury, soft‑tissue, etc.).
- Trial experience: many cases settle, but a lawyer who won’t hesitate to go to trial generally gets better offers from insurers.
- Communication: you want prompt responses, clear explanations, and a lawyer who involves you in decisions.
- Track record and reputation: ask about average recoveries, recent results, and client references.
- Resources: serious firms advance medical and litigation costs and can handle expert witnesses if needed.
- Fee structure and expenses: most work on contingency (no fees unless you recover). Confirm percentage and how costs are handled.

Questions to ask in a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the results?
- What’s your success rate and trial experience?
- Who will handle my case day‑to‑day (attorney vs paralegal)?
- How do you charge? What percentage and what expenses will be deducted?
- How long do you expect this case to take?
- Can you provide client references or recent verdicts/settlements?
- Will you advance medical or litigation costs?

What you should do right now (if you haven’t already)
- Get prompt medical care and follow treatment instructions — medical records are essential evidence.
- Preserve evidence: photos of the scene/car, damage, injuries; witness names/contact info; police report number.
- Don’t post details or admit fault on social media.
- Don’t sign medical releases or give recorded statements to insurers before consulting a lawyer.
- Notify your insurer but limit the information to the basics.

Documents to bring to the lawyer consultation
- Police report (or report number)
- Photos/videos of the crash, car damage, injuries
- Medical records, bills, and provider names
- Insurance information (your policy and other parties’ if known)
- Correspondence from insurers
- Any witness contact info
- Paystubs/records showing lost wages

Timing and legal deadlines
- California personal injury statute of limitations is generally 2 years from the date of injury (often 2 years for bodily injury, 3 years for property in some cases). If a government agency is involved, you may need to file an administrative claim much sooner (often within 6 months). Start now — don’t wait.

How to find and vet attorneys
- Get 3 consultations and compare answers.
- Check the State Bar of California for license status and discipline history (www.calbar.ca.gov).
- Read recent client reviews (Google, Yelp) and professional ratings (Martindale‑Hubbell, Avvo).
- Prefer local attorneys who practice in Alameda or Contra Costa County; they’ll know local judges and opposing counsel.

If you’d like, I can
- Find and list 3–5 well‑reviewed personal injury attorneys in Pleasanton / Tri‑Valley with contact info and short notes about their practice areas and reviews.
- Prepare a short script of what to say and which documents to hand over at a first consultation.

Which would you prefer? If you want specific attorney names, tell me whether you prefer a solo attorney, small firm, or larger firm, and any special needs (catastrophic injury, neck/back, uninsured driver, wrongful death).
